title: FIA condemns online abuse of F1 stewards after Colapinto’s Dutch GP penalties
content:
The FIA has condemned a wave of online abuse aimed at its race stewards following penalties handed down at Sunday’s Dutch Grand Prix.

In a statement Tuesday, posted on X alongside the United Against Online Abuse coalition, the governing body said officials had been targeted after applying sanctions in line with FIA statutes. “Disagreement with decisions is part of sport, but it must never justify threats or personal attacks,” the post read. The coalition was founded in 2023 by FIA president Mohammed Ben Sulayem after a steward was harassed following the United States Grand Prix.

The Dutch GP gave the stewards plenty to do. In a race won by McLaren’s Lando Norris, Racing Bulls rookie Arvid Lindblad and Alpine’s Franco Colapinto took penalty points on their superlicences, finishing 12th and 14th. Lindblad received a drive-through for passing Pierre Gasly under double-waved yellows on lap one, with stewards citing track debris as a mitigating factor.

Colapinto was given a drive-through for an opening-lap pass on Yuki Tsunoda under yellows that became a red flag after Max Verstappen crashed, then a further 10-second penalty. Red Bull’s Liam Lawson took 10 seconds for speeding under the same yellows, though it did not change his seventh place. Colapinto has four penalty points on his superlicence — 12 in 12 months brings an automatic one-race ban.

The FIA did not detail the abuse, but reports described a flood of hostile posts aimed at stewards, some claiming Colapinto was disciplined for his nationality and alleging bias against non-British drivers — an accusation undercut by the punishment for Lindblad, who is British and received an identical penalty for a near-identical offense.

The officiating also drew ire from one of Colapinto’s commercial partners. Sean Summers, chief marketing officer of Mercado Libre, posted a scathing critique of the stewards before deleting it. Summers tagged the FIA’s official X account and wrote: “The stewards are killing the integrity of F1. This season, they are proving to be horrible and impacting race results. Incompetence? Dishonesty? Both? Something is seriously broken in that organisation’s culture.”

FIA spokesperson Cameron Kelleher confirmed to The Athletic that the FIA is assessing legal options regarding Summers’ allegations.

Alpine’s response was more measured, calling the yellow-flag penalties harsh but consistently applied, and a learning opportunity for the team.

This is not the first time Colapinto’s fanbase has been at the center of such a wave. In May, the Argentine publicly urged his supporters to show restraint after Tsunoda was deluged with abusive Instagram comments, many in Spanish, following a practice incident at Imola where Colapinto impeded him. Jack Doohan, the driver Colapinto replaced at Alpine, has also been a repeated target. Colapinto has acknowledged it himself, saying, “We need to put a limit on it.”

The season resumes at Monza for the Italian Grand Prix, round 13, with first practice on September 4.
